cards.explanation: The answer is that Herod arrests another believer. Herod, the king, saw that killing James pleased the Jews, and he "…proceeded to seize Peter…" (Acts 12:3). Peter is one of Jesus' twelve apostles (Matthew 10:2). I think this is a heavy turn, friends, because one hard act rolls right into the next.

The answer is Passover. Acts 12:4 says Herod "…intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover." So the timing is already set in his mind. Peter is sitting in that prison with a clock running.

The answer is True! Acts 12:5 says that while Peter was kept in prison, "…the church was fervently praying to God for him." Peter is locked up, and the church is praying hard. That sentence sits right in the middle of a very tense story.

The answer is sleeping! Acts 12:6 says Peter was "…sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains…" The trial is the next day, and he's out cold. Me, I'd be staring at the ceiling counting cookie sheets.
The answer is True. The angel tells Peter, "Get up quickly." Then "…the chains fell off his wrists." (Acts 12:7). Two chains were holding him (Acts 12:6), and they came off.

The answer is that Peter thinks he's only seeing a vision. Acts 12:9 says Peter followed the angel out, "…but he was unaware that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was only seeing a vision." So he's walking out of prison and thinks it's only a vision. I'd be pinching myself the whole way.

The answer is that the gate opens for them by itself! Acts 12:10 says they passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city, which "…opened for them by itself." Then they went outside. That's some gate, friends.

The answer is False. Acts 12:10 says that after they walked one block, "…the angel suddenly left him." Then Peter came to himself in the street (Acts 12:11). Acts 12:12 says that once he realized what had happened, he went to the house.

The answer is that the Lord sent His angel to rescue him. Peter says, "Now I know for sure that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s grasp…" (Acts 12:11). Before, he thought it was a vision. Now it's clear to him that it's real.

The answer is that Rhoda runs inside and leaves the gate shut. Rhoda, the servant girl at Mary's house, was "…so overjoyed that she forgot to open the gate, but ran inside…" (Acts 12:14). I've forgotten plenty of things when I got excited, but a whole gate takes talent. Peter was standing out there the whole time.

The answer is False. Acts 12:15 says they told her, "You are out of your mind…" When she kept insisting, they said, "It must be his angel." These are the same people who had gathered to pray (Acts 12:12), and they still need a minute.

The answer is astounded! Acts 12:16 says Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, "…they were astounded." Earlier they had told Rhoda, "You are out of your mind…" (Acts 12:15). He was standing right there at the door, just like Rhoda said.

The answer is that Peter leaves for another place. After telling them to send word to James and the brothers, Peter "…left for another place." (Acts 12:17). The text doesn't say where. I'll leave it open, same as the verse does.

The answer is that the guards be executed. After Herod searched for Peter without finding him, "…he examined the guards and ordered that they be executed." (Acts 12:19). I think this one is heavy, friends, so I'll let it sit. It tells us what kind of ruler Herod is.

The answer is food. Acts 12:20 says Herod was in a "…furious dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon…" and they asked for peace "…because their region depended on the king’s country for food." Tyre and Sidon needed what Herod's country supplied, so they weren't about to stay in a fight. When the folks who feed you are mad at you, you make peace FAST.

The answer is that it's the voice of a god. The people shout, "This is the voice of a god, not a man!" (Acts 12:22). That's a lot of praise to pile on a man in royal robes. And they said it about a man, not about God.

The answer is glory. Acts 12:23 says that "…because Herod did not give glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down…" The crowd had just called his voice the voice of a god (Acts 12:22). The text gives that reason itself.

The answer is Jerusalem. Acts 12:25 says Barnabas and Saul "…had fulfilled their mission to Jerusalem…" and then returned. They brought John, also called Mark, back with them. Mission finished, and they came home with company.
